newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong considers whether Taiwan flags can fly.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong considers whether Taiwan flags can fly.

text.p: Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Thursday his government was considering whether to allow Nationalist Chinese flags to be flown in the territory on October 10, Taiwan's national day.
"The government is actively studying it," he told reporters in answer to a question, stressing that there could be no deviation from the "one-China policy".
In the past, Taiwan's national day has been marked with flags hoisted prominently in the territory.
Tung's comments came just five weeks after this former British colony returned to communist Chinese rule.
Under its new mini-constitution, the Basic Law, Hong Kong must observe the "one-China" principle.
Communist-ruled China regards arch-rival Taiwan as a renegade province and opposes it establishing diplomatic relations with other countries.
Most countries with diplomatic links to Taiwan have shut their Hong Kong consulates in line with China's demands following the resumption of sovereignty on July 1, officials said on Thursday.

Taiwan has only 30 diplomatic partners, mostly poor Latin American or African nations, after fighting a losing battle with China for diplomatic recognition since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
That number will fall to 29 next year when South Africa, Taipei's largest ally, switches formal recognition to Beijing.
